newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up, ignoring IMF news.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up, ignoring IMF news.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Monday with the market shrugging off news that an International Monetary Fund mission would leave Moscow without deciding whether to pay the next tranche of a loan, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 0.37 percent to 191.94 on a low $10.08 million in volume.

"The IMF news is one of the routine issues," said Alexander Lobanov, a trader from Rinaco-Plus. "It is like with the Chechen war -- in general everyone is concerned, but the market moves regardless of what is happening there."
The market would not react until the IMF takes a final decision on the Russian loan, he said.

An IMF mission will leave Moscow on Monday without taking a decision on whether Russia should receive the latest tranche of its $10 billion loan, but will return early next week for further discussions, a Russian participant in the talks said.
Traders said the market fell in early trade on local profit-taking and edged up later with Western orders coming in only for shares backed by American Depositary Receipts.
"Big foreign investors are waiting for the IMF decision and until it takes it we are in for a quiet market on local operations," said Alexei Goncharov, an analyst at Russian Brokerage House.
He said most Russian operators had expected the IMF not pay the November tranche and had already discounted this possibility.

Samaraenergo rose to $0.43 from $0.36 at Friday's close, Gazprom edged up to $0.355 from $0.334, Novosibirskenergo rose to $3.47 from $3.00 at Thursday's close when it was last traded, Mosenergo was $0.990 after $0.997 and UES fell to $0.0820 from $0.0825.
